solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ambassador is one in charge taking on supporter with skill and tact

parts.note: an ambassador is an example of a diplomat
an ally is someone who backs you

explanation.surface: An ambassador who runs things wins over a backer through deft diplomacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with skill and tact in dealings with people is the adverb's exact sense.

clue.text: Unusual item takes in the press etc on the spot

indicators.note: takes in shows the shuffled letters wrap around another piece
unusual tells us the letters of item are set out in an odd order

parts.note: the press, broadcasting and the like are the media

explanation.surface: An odd news item gets picked up by journalists straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' tempts as a verb, but 'the press etc' names the news outlets collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done on the spot happens at once, without delay.

clue.text: Partly assimilate Romanians in the future

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark about absorbing people from Romania, to be done some time ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe a time after the present, synonyms for afterwards.

clue.text: Required a president mostly propped up by a rightwinger

indicators.note: in a down clue, propped up by puts the next pieces underneath the first
mostly here trims the president's surname well short of its full length

parts.note: Nelson Mandela was president of South Africa
a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: A head of state who could only stay in office with the backing of a conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' is generous here: MANDELA loses three letters, ELA, not just its last one. Tory is the nickname for Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mandatory is compulsory, a direct synonym of required.

clue.text: A bit of a confused state

indicators.note: confused tells us the letters of state are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admits to being slightly muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun phrase: 'a taste of' something means a small sample of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sample or sip of something is a taste of it.

clue.text: Continuous rest during extremely critical first part of written assignment

indicators.note: during means one piece sits within the other
extremely asks for only the outermost letters of critical

parts.note: ease is relaxation or rest

indicators.note: first part of keeps the opening letters of the word and drops its tail

parts.note: an essay is a written assignment set for students

explanation.surface: Endless breaks appear in the harshest opening section of homework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first part of' trims the synonym for the written assignment rather than picking letters from a printed word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceaseless and continuous both mean going on without stopping, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Head off escape at dawn

indicators.note: head off says the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: flight is the act of fleeing or escaping

explanation.surface: A plan to cut off a breakout at daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like a verb meaning intercept, but it removes the F from FLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: First light is daybreak, so light alone can stand for dawn.

clue.text: Longed to say why journalist has a navy sweetheart

indicators.note: to say means the word is heard rather than read, giving a single letter with that sound

parts.note: the letter Y is pronounced like the word why

indicators.note: has means the journalist piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
RN is the abbreviation for Royal Navy
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: An editor explains a fondness for a sailor girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' means the heart of 'sweet'; 'has' means the journalist holds the other three pieces, so the order differs from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long for something intensely, a direct synonym.

clue.text: After a short break, worker is available

indicators.note: after places the worker piece behind the break piece

parts.note: vac is short for vacation, a break
the worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: Following a brief holiday, an employee is free again.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacant seat or post is one that is free to be taken.

clue.text: Acknowledge not all plead mitigation

indicators.note: not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: In court, not every defendant offers excuses for leniency.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to acknowledge it as true.

clue.text: "Remembrance of Things Past" is a long novel about tiresome adolescent initially

indicators.note: about shows the rearranged letters go around the next piece
novel as an adjective means new, so the letters take a new arrangement
initially takes the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Proust's famous book is lengthy fiction about a dull teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges IS A LONG to NOSLGIA, and 'about' puts TA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a wistful recollection of the past, which Proust's title describes.

clue.text: Country girl embraces king after empty afternoon

indicators.note: after means the girl piece follows the afternoon piece
empty removes the inner letters, leaving just the outer ones
embraces means one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: Dora is a girl's name
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A rural lass hugs a monarch after an idle afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a small country in the Pyrenees between France and Spain.

clue.text: Former tennis star appearing for football team

parts.note: Chris Evert was a leading tennis player of the 1970s and 80s
on means performing or appearing, as on stage

explanation.surface: A retired tennis player turns out for a football side.
explanation.walkthrough: EVERTON is a football club in Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a Premier League football club from Liverpool.

clue.text: Quarrel about concealing Republican tricks

indicators.note: concealing means the reversed word holds another piece inside
about here means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a spat is a small quarrel

explanation.surface: An argument about hiding a party member's dirty tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SPAT into TAPS, and 'concealing' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Traps are snares or tricks set to catch someone out.

clue.text: Distrust cop I mixed with in South America previously

indicators.note: previously places these letters before the rest

parts.note: US stands for the United States, America

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A policeman admits being wary of something going on earlier in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two fodder pieces; 'previously' puts South America's letters in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspicion is a feeling of mistrust toward someone.

clue.text: No writer finished without fixed deadlines

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing or no
a pen is an instrument for writing
ended means finished

explanation.surface: An author with no pen finishes without any deadline pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-ended arrangement has no set limit or end date.

clue.text: Spirited opener has no work to achieve first century

indicators.note: has no means the following piece is removed

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
to get something is to achieve or obtain it
I is the Roman numeral one, first
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: A lively batsman fails to work hard enough to reach a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opener is the first batsman and a century is a hundred runs; removing OP from OPENER leaves ENER.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirited and energetic both describe someone full of life and vigour.

clue.text: Used door at end for keeping smells away

indicators.note: used in the sense of worn or knocked about, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A second-hand door at the far end blocks odours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used' looks like an adjective for the door but rearranges DOOR AT END.
explanation.definitionFit: A deodorant is a product applied to mask body odour.

clue.text: Permitted a design of any kind you like

parts.note: free means allowed or permitted
a style is a design or fashion

explanation.surface: Any design is allowed, whatever you like.
explanation.definitionFit: Freestyle describes something without fixed rules, done any way you prefer.

clue.text: Hat cover protects air cadets

indicators.note: protects means one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a flap is a covering piece
ATC is the Air Training Corps, the British air cadets

explanation.surface: A cover keeps young air force recruits safe.
explanation.walkthrough: ATC is the Air Training Corps, Britain's air cadet organisation; a FLAT CAP is a soft round cloth cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat cap is a type of cloth cap worn in Britain.

clue.text: Jar of spawn?

parts.note: a jolt, and also a playful split of the last word into a letter plus a word for pledging goods

explanation.surface: A container of frogs' eggs, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jar' is a jolt, not a pot. The question mark licenses splitting 'spawn' as S + PAWN, and HOCK is slang for pawn, so S-HOCK is a cryptic 's-pawn'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jar is a sudden jolt or unpleasant surprise, a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Core of vegetable turnover contains peeled turnip

indicators.note: contains means the reversed word holds the next piece
turnover means the word is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: a leek is a vegetable

indicators.note: peeled removes outer layers, leaving the middle letters

explanation.surface: The heart of a vegetable pie holds a pared turnip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' tempts as a pastry beside vegetable, but it signals reversal; 'peeled' strips the root down to its two central letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the central or essential part of something.

clue.text: Fix for dad to go back east say

indicators.note: to go back means the word is reversed

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
east is an example of a compass point

explanation.surface: Arranging for a father to return eastward.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint a time is to fix or set it.

clue.text: Bear goes back to sleep with Russian's agreement

indicators.note: goes back means the word is reversed

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
da is Russian for yes

explanation.surface: A bear returns to hibernate with Moscow's approval.
explanation.definitionFit: The panda is a black-and-white bear from China.

clue.text: Support most of the enforcement mechanisms

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Backing most of the means of enforcing the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: A law with teeth has the power to enforce it.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth in the sense of powers to compel compliance.

clue.text: Appeal of Guardian leader beat the FT's!

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of the word

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
the FT setter refers to the paper's own as ours

explanation.surface: A rival paper's editorial outdoes the Financial Times in appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is an attractive or exciting appeal.

clue.text: Terrible rise of Washington flu variation

indicators.note: rise of in a down clue means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: WA is the abbreviation for Washington state

indicators.note: variation means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful increase in a new strain of influenza in Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful and terrible are synonyms for very bad.

clue.text: Certain of swindle by half of dentists about front fillings

parts.note: a con is a swindle

indicators.note: front keeps just the opening of the word, here its first two letters
half of keeps the first four of the eight letters

explanation.surface: Sure of a scam in which some dentists charge for front-tooth fillings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is best read as a loose link; the pieces simply run CON, FI, DENT, and the blogger also found the construction awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Being confident of something means being sure or certain of it.

clue.text: Put together the conclusion after Friday morning

indicators.note: after places the conclusion after the preceding letters

parts.note: am means morning

indicators.note: conclusion picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Wrapping things up after Friday morning.
explanation.definitionFit: To frame something is to put together or construct it.

clue.text: Dark bar makes alcoholic pant with ecstasy

indicators.note: makes means the letters are made into something new

parts.note: E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A dark chocolate bar makes a drunkard breathe heavily with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges ALCOHOLIC PANT; E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain is the British term for dark, unsweetened-by-milk confectionery, sold in slabs.
